What the differences mean

Dealectric does not test units. Every figure below comes from the maker's US store on 2026-11-17 or from a named reviewer's measurement. Price per Wh divides the price you pay through our link (the checkout code is already applied) by the battery's rated Wh. The store price without the code is shown next to it.

  • ALLPOWERS R3500 + 600 W: $1,753.93 ÷ 3,168 Wh = $0.55 per Wh (store $1,993.10 ÷ 3,168 = $0.63).
  • BLUETTI Elite 400 + 2× 200 W: $1,804.05 ÷ 3,840 Wh = $0.47 (store $1,899.00 → $0.49). It is $398 less than buying the same parts separately.
  • BLUETTI Elite 300 + 2× 200 W: $1,614.05 ÷ 3,014.4 Wh = $0.54 (store $1,699.00 → $0.56). It is $298 less than the parts.
  • BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 + 2× 200 W: $1,424.05 ÷ 2,073.6 Wh = $0.69 (store $1,499.00 → $0.72).
  • Anker SOLIX F3000 + 400 W: $2,599.99 ÷ 3,072 Wh = $0.85 at Anker's store.
  • Sun hours = battery Wh ÷ panel W. For example, 3,168 ÷ 600 = 5.3 h and 3,840 ÷ 400 = 9.6 h. This assumes the panels deliver their full rating, which they rarely do, so a real refill takes longer. A kit that needs more sun hours than your site gets in a day won't refill from empty in one day.

Price per Wh, sun hours and what the batteries actually delivered

Price per Wh is what you pay for each watt-hour of storage. Sun hours tell you whether the included panels can refill that storage in a day. Read together, they explain the pick. The R3500 + 600 W kit costs $0.55 per Wh, about 35% less than the F3000 kit's $0.85. Its 600 W panel is also the largest in this table relative to its battery, so it needs 5.3 h of rated sun against the F3000 kit's 7.7 h. ALLPOWERS rates the R3500 for over 3,500 charging cycles and up to 2,000 W of solar input, so you can add panels later. {buy:allpowers-r3500-sp039-solar-kit}

Rated Wh is not what reaches your appliances, because the inverter uses some of it. Notebookcheck (Marcus Schwarten) drained three of these stations at a light, steady load with the same method. The Anker SOLIX F3000 gave about 2,500 Wh at 200 W, 81% of 3,072 Wh. The BLUETTI Elite 300 gave about 2,650 Wh at just over 200 W, just under 88% of 3,014.4 Wh. The BLUETTI Elite 400 gave about 3,130 Wh at about 250 W, just under 82% of 3,840 Wh. StorageReview measured 1.91 kWh from the Elite 200 V2, about 92% of 2,073.6 Wh. Dividing each kit's price by the energy it delivered:

  • Elite 400 + 2× 200 W: $1,804.05 ÷ 3,130 Wh = $0.58 per delivered Wh.
  • Elite 300 + 2× 200 W: $1,614.05 ÷ 2,650 Wh = $0.61.
  • Elite 200 V2 + 2× 200 W: $1,424.05 ÷ 1,910 Wh = $0.75.
  • F3000 + 400 W: $2,599.99 ÷ 2,500 Wh = $1.04.

We could not source a named lab's drain test for the R3500, so its row uses rated figures only. If you can wait for BLUETTI's dispatch dates, the Elite 400 + 2× 200 W kit still costs the least per Wh, measured or rated: {buy:bluetti-elite-400-2x200w-solar-kit}

Where we drew the line: every kit in the table cost $3,000 or less at its price on 2026-11-17. Left out:

  • BLUETTI Apex 300 + 2× 500 W, at $3,134.05 through our link.
  • The EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra solar generator. EcoFlow's store showed only the lowest variant's price that day, not the kit with panels.
  • Jackery's kits, whose panels were on pre-order until Nov 28 to Dec 15.
  • The ALLPOWERS R3500 + 400 W kit, whose store price changed between our reads this week.

Not recommended

BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 or Elite 400 with 2× 350 W panels. Here is the arithmetic from BLUETTI's own figures:

  • BLUETTI lists its 350 W panel at 33 V open-circuit. Two in series make 66 V, which is over the 12–60 V solar input on both stations, and cold weather pushes the voltage higher. So the two panels can only be wired in parallel.
  • Parallel wiring needs an MC4 Y-branch cable that isn't in the box. BLUETTI's own Y-branch ($39) showed sold out on 2026-11-17.
  • Even in parallel, the 20 A input cap holds the pair under 20 A × 33 V = 660 W, so the 700 W of panels can't all be used.

The 2× 200 W versions of the same stations cost less and can be wired in series within the 60 V limit. If you want about 700 W of panels on a BLUETTI station, look at one with two solar inputs, such as the Apex 300.

The Anker SOLIX F3000's 3,600 W figure is the TT-30R RV port and the total across outlets. Each household NEMA 5-20R outlet is rated 2,400 W max.
